chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Safwan and al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the man who plays with his wife until he ejaculates while he is in ihram without sexual intercourse, or does that in the month of Ramadan, so he said: 'On both of them is the expiation like that upon the one who has intercourse.'
And whoever listens to the speech of a woman or listens to a couple having intercourse without seeing them, and then ejaculates, there is no expiation upon him. Narrated.

key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: one in the state of ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj/Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a man in ihram who ejaculates without intercourse?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in the context of Ihram violations, establishing that non-coital ejaculation (maniy) incurs the same expiation (kaffarah) as full intercourse, a key distinction in Shia fiqh. The hadith further clarifies the concept of 'hearing' (tasammu') as a cause for ejaculation, noting that mere auditory stimulation without visual confirmation or direct intercourse exempts the individual from penalty, highlighting the juristic focus on the mode of sensory engagement.
